fresh flow down the left half of the frame from crown to root-line, running off the top and bottom edges, a bulging leading edge as deep as a cone is long still moving, its top skin already wrinkling and matte over a body that is wet and mirror-bright pale honey, greenish-clear at the thin margins, one trapped bubble the size of a grape stopped halfway down its face

hanging sheet stretched between two trunks filling the entire lower two-thirds and running off both sides, a metre and a half across, thick enough to sag belly-downward, its surface skinned over and matte with fine dust, pale honey shading to dark treacle where the rolled bottom edge is heaviest, one vertical crease where it nearly tore and healed with a paler seam

hardened boulder of old resin welded to the trunk where it grew, swelling out of the bark at the base and sunk into the needle-litter at its foot, filling the whole lower-left corner and running off the left and bottom edges, as big as a crouching animal, milky and clouded inside, rust where bark is suspended near its core, its outside furred with stuck pine dust and one crack wide enough to hold shadow

stretched thread dropping from a branch across the right half of the frame, running off the top and bottom edges, a strand no thicker than a horsetail stem but taut and nearly transparent, pale honey, a heavy drop at its lower end the size of a plum, still wet and mirror-bright, a tiny bark flake caught inside the drop like a dark comma

bead row along the underside of a horizontal branch filling the upper third and running off both sides, a couple of dozen swelling drops at wildly uneven spacing, some crowded almost touching and some a frond-width apart, the biggest the size of a plum and the smallest barely a seed, wet and mirror-bright pale honey, the fattest ones near the centre beginning to elongate downward under their own weight, one drop at the far left already clouding milky at its crown

torn scar on a trunk filling the right two-thirds of the frame and running off the top and right edges, the old crust dark and dull as dried bark, split open to show fresh resin welling through it bright and mirror-wet, dark treacle at the thick well, greenish-clear where it thins at the scar lips, a single conifer needle standing upright in the fresh welling surface

sagging shelf of old flows swelling out from a trunk base, occupying the centre-left and running off the bottom edge, one lopsided mass where three runs of different ages have piled onto each other at no regular interval, the lowest lobe grey and crazed with age, a broad pale-honey bulge slumped over it well off-centre, the newest run still wet and mirror-bright and spilling down one side only, a healed crack showing as a paler seam across the bulge

pool on the ground in the lower third running off both sides and the bottom edge, spread flat where a flow ran off the trunk, its surface skinned over and matte, dusted with fallen needles lying flat and preserved in the skin, pale honey at the thin edges, dark treacle in the deepest centre, one small air pocket under the skin making a white blister

split nodule half-buried in the needle-litter where it fell from the trunk above, lower-right corner, running off the right and bottom edges, a cone-sized lump with litter banked against one side and a fern stem growing past it, its upper crust dull and crazed the colour of old bark, the freshly cracked face turned up to the light water-clear and mirror-bright, one grain of grit caught on the line between dull outside and clear inside

glazed flank of a trunk filling the left half of the frame and running off the top, bottom, and left edges, one continuous smooth coat a centimetre thick, wet-looking and mirror-bright, pale honey where it is thinnest, shading to dark treacle in the wide central channel where the flow was heaviest, a run that split around a buried knot and rejoined below it in a smooth lobe

fresh flow in the upper-right corner running off the top and right edges, thick as poured honey, its leading edge a heavy rounded lip as deep as a cone is long and still moving, the top skin wrinkling and going matte where it has begun to set, body beneath still mirror-bright pale honey, one bubble the size of a grape stopped just below the wrinkling surface

hanging sheet between two trunks across the upper half running off both sides and the top edge, thick enough to distort the dark trunks behind it into smeared columns, its bottom edge heavy and rolled like a hem, surface skinned over and dusted with fine grit, pale honey at the top where it is stretched thinnest, near-black where the rolled bottom edge is thickest

hardened boulder grown out from the bark at a trunk base, still joined to the trunk by a broad neck of old resin, filling the lower-right corner and running off the right and bottom edges, as wide as a fallen log, its surface matted with compacted grit and old needles, crazed inside with white cracks branching like dry riverbeds, rust where bark plates are sealed in its body

stretched thread across the left half of the frame running off the top and bottom edges, nearly invisible where it is thinnest, thickening at a midpoint into a small lens-shaped bead, pale honey shading to greenish-clear at its narrowest, a heavy drop at the bottom still wet and mirror-bright, a tiny bark fragment sealed inside the lens like a dark island

bead row under a branch filling the lower third and running off both sides, each drop fat and round as a marble, wet and mirror-bright, the row going pale honey at the outer ends and shading to dark treacle at the centre where the branch weeps most heavily, two adjacent drops in the centre touching and beginning to merge into one larger oval, their shared wall still visible as a faint seam

torn scar across the upper-left quadrant running off the top and left edges, the old crust thick and dark, chewed open in a long diagonal split, fresh resin welling out in a slow bright bead along the full length of the split, mirror-wet and pale honey, darkening to dark treacle where it pools in the lowest part of the gash, the crust on either side pitted and dusty

lumpy accumulation of old flows at a trunk base, centre of the frame, running off the bottom edge, no two lobes the same size or shape and none of them level, a wide grey crazed foot at the ground, a milky mass bulging asymmetrically out to the left above it, a mirror-bright fresh tongue running down the right side and out past the bottom edge, a fragment of bark sealed in the milky part well off-centre

pool in the lower-left corner running off the left and bottom edges, spread nearly flat, its skin matte and holding a light dusting of grit, two conifer needles half-submerged and slightly tilted as though still settling, pale honey at the margins thinning to nearly colourless, dark treacle in the thickest central depression, the skin slightly puckered where a small air pocket pushes from below

split nodule lying in the litter against a root, lower-left corner, running off the left and bottom edges, the size of two cones together with needles and a broken twig stuck to its damp underside, its crazed exterior the colour of old bark, the broken face water-clear and mirror-bright where it has turned toward the light, one bubble sealed inside like a round eye

glazed flank in the right half of the frame running off the top, right, and bottom edges, the resin coat a full centimetre thick across the entire visible face of the trunk, mirror-bright and wet-looking, pale honey where it coats the high ridges of the bark, dark treacle pooled in the long grooves, a run that split around a raised knot and rejoined in a smooth teardrop shape below it

fresh flow in the lower-left corner running off the left and bottom edges, a thick slow tongue as deep as a cone is long at its leading edge, the top skin wrinkling into fine parallel ridges where it has begun to set, the body beneath mirror-bright pale honey, greenish-clear where it thins at the sides, a crack in the setting skin that has healed with a paler seam across its centre

hardened boulder sunk into the forest floor at the foot of a trunk, moss creeping up one flank and litter drifted against the other, centre-bottom and running off the bottom edge, as big as a resting animal, its outer crust dull and matte with grit and needle fragments pressed into it, cloudy inside with white cracks showing through, a plate of bark sealed just under the surface

stretched thread from a high branch filling the right third and running off the top and bottom edges, a single long strand the width of a horsetail stem, taut under the weight of its own hanging drop, nearly transparent pale honey, the drop at the bottom fat and mirror-bright and still pulling the strand a little longer, a grain of dark grit sealed inside the drop at its equator

bead row under a branch in the upper-right corner running off the top and right edges, the drops scattered at no regular interval along it, three crowded together at one knot and a long bare stretch beyond them, the smallest the size of a pea and the largest nearly the size of a walnut, all wet and mirror-bright, pale honey shading to dark treacle at the largest, one drop showing a single conifer needle pressed flat against its surface from the inside

torn scar filling the centre and upper-left running off the top and left edges, a wide ragged split in the trunk, the old crust on either side dark and pitted with old dried drips, fresh resin pouring through in a broad bright tongue, mirror-wet, pale honey at the surface, dark treacle in the depth of the wound where it is thickest, a run already beginning to skin at its lower lip
